title: SIG questionnaire walkthrough - Aperture Bank
next_steps: Redwood to upload SIG/CAIQ completed responses to shared Box folder by 2026-07-14
Customer to provide list of additional evidence requests by 2026-07-17
Schedule follow-up deep-dive on KMS integration with Aperture infra week of 2026-07-20
action_items: Jared Kim: upload completed SIG spreadsheet and link to evidence bundle (due 2026-07-14)
Priya Nair: provide architecture diagram and KMS integration notes (due 2026-07-16)
Ethan Brooks: send Aperture's SOC 2 questions that need clarification (due 2026-07-17)
summary: Walkthrough of Aperture Bank's vendor risk SIG/CAIQ. Covered SOC 2/ISO posture, SSO/RBAC, audit logging, data residency, and encryption/KMS integration. Redwood to deliver SIG responses and evidence bundle; follow-up on KMS key management and regional data residency clarifications.
topics: Data residency and VPC deployment options
transcript:
[00:00] Jared (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, I'll start - Jared Kim from Redwood.
[00:05] Priya (Redwood SE): Priya Nair here, I'll run through the SIG answers and technical bits.
[00:09] Sarah (Aperture - CISO): Sarah Cole, Aperture CISO. Tom, Maya and Ethan are here as well.
[00:14] Tom (Aperture - SecOps): Hey.
[00:16] Maya (Aperture - Procurement): Hi all.
[00:18] Ethan (Aperture - Cloud): Ethan here.
[00:22] Jared: Great. Goal for today is to walk through the SIG/CAIQ questionnaire, call out where we need evidence, and surface any gaps around SOC 2, ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logging, data residency and KMS. We'll note action items and timelines.
[00:35] Priya: Alright jumping in - on the SIG spreadsheet we prefilled a bunch of answers. Some are straightforward yes/no, others need an evidence artefact or a sample config. For example, SOC 2 attestation: we have our latest SOC 2 Type II report from 2025 and we'll link that in the evidence bundle.
[00:50] Sarah: Quick question - how do you handle subservice orgs? Our procurement team always wants to know what third parties Redwood uses for hosting and ops.
[00:58] Priya: Good call. We use public cloud providers for hosted deployments - we list AWS and GCP as subservice orgs. We include their respective SOC reports and CAIQ pieces where applicable. In the SIG we map controls to service providers. Sometimes the transcription tools cough up "GPC" instead of GCP, sorry for that in the doc.
[01:15] Tom: For the evidence bundle, do you share raw logs or redacted samples? Our policy doesn't allow full PII leakage.
[01:22] Jared: We typically provide redacted log samples and templates for audit logs - timestamps, event types, retention policy screenshots. Full raw logs aren't shared. We'll mark that as an evidence note.
[01:30] Ethan: On encryption/keys - does Redwood manage keys or do you integrate with customer KMS/HSM? Aperture wants BYOK ideally.
[01:37] Priya: We support both. For Redwood Hosted customers we can manage keys and offer KMS integration; for Private deployments VPC/on-prem we can integrate with customer KMS via customer-managed keys (BYOK) - we documented typical flows in the KMS appendix. For the SIG question about key rotation, we noted automated rotation for our managed keys and support for customer rotation schedules when integrated.
[01:55] Sarah: Can you confirm FIPS or HSM usage if we require HSM-backed keys?
[02:00] Priya: We can support HSM-backed keys via our KMS integrations - we call out HSM support in the evidence notes and can provide architecture diagrams. We'll need to coordinate with your cloud team for the private connection.
[02:10] Maya: On SSO, we saw "supports SAML and OIDC" in the doc. Can you do SCIM for user provisioning?
[02:16] Jared: Yes, we support SAML for SSO and SCIM for provisioning in the Console. We'll attach the SSO guide and an example SAML metadata file.
[02:25] Ethan: How granular is RBAC? Can we map to existing groups/roles?
[02:28] Priya: Role-based access controls support org-level roles and token-scoped permissions; you can map to your IdP groups via SCIM or group mappings. We typically provide a sample RBAC matrix.
[02:38] Tom: Audit logs - retention defaults and ability to ship logs to our SIEM?
[02:42] Priya: Default audit retention is 90 days in the Console, with options for longer retention as an add-on. We can forward logs to your SIEM via syslog or customer-managed S3 buckets for long-term retention. We'll include the forwarding config in the evidence.
[02:58] Sarah: Data residency - Aperture requires data at rest for EU customers to remain in EU regions. Do you have regional deployments?
[03:04] Jared: Yes, Redwood supports region pinning for hosted and dedicated models. For full EU residency we can run in EU regions and provide Private deployment options (VPC or on-prem) for stricter controls. We'll mark the SIG questions about data center locations as "requires evidence" and include our region list.
[03:20] Maya: On breach notification - what's the timeframe you commit to?
[03:24] Priya: Our policy is 72 hours for confirmed breaches, and we provide a timeline for incident reports; we'll include the incident response playbook excerpt.
[03:34] Ethan: A few technical clarifications - KV cache question was mis-transcribed in the doc as "CV cache" - we use KV cache for model token caching; does that change any data residency concerns?
[03:44] Priya: KV cache exists in memory per request and can be configured to avoid persistent storage. For customers with strict residency we recommend Private deployment where cache lifecycles are fully under customer control.
[03:56] Jared: There's a SIG item on encryption in transit - TLS versions and cipher suites, we have a published list in the security whitepaper.
[04:04] Priya: Also multi-tenant encryption boundaries - we note per-tenant isolation for tokens and ephemeral caches; it's in the documentation.
[04:12] Tom: Evidence around SOC 2 controls - can you provide the control mapping and sample test procedures?
[04:18] Jared: We'll include the SOC 2 mapping spreadsheet and sample control test outputs. The SOC report itself is included but redacted for customer names.
[04:26] Maya: Procurement needs proof of insurance and indemnity language. Where does that sit?
[04:30] Jared: We'll attach our certificate of insurance and standard contract language; legal can follow up if Aperture requests edits.
[04:36] Ethan: Is there a way to run an on-prem POC for performance and audit validation?
[04:41] Priya: Yes we support POCs on Dedicated/Dedicated Private - we can set up a timeboxed POC with restricted dataset and run through the security checks. That typically takes 2-4 weeks to provision depending on infra.
[04:53] Sarah: About the SIG sheet itself, I noticed some items are marked as "partially implemented" - can you walk through one example?
[04:59] Priya: Sure, for continuous vulnerability scanning we list automated scans and occasional manual pen tests. The "partial" flag is for features where a customer-managed component is an option - e.g., we do internal scanning, but customers can run their own scanning in Private deployments; we'll clarify in the note.
[05:12] Tom: For logging to our SIEM, what's the delivery method and authentication?
[05:16] Priya: We can push via TLS syslog with mutual TLS or store logs to a customer S3 with signed URLs. We'll document the auth methods and sample configs.
[05:26] Maya: Any blockers from Redwood's side for providing evidence? We want things fast.
[05:30] Jared: We typically can turn around the SIG responses and evidence bundle within 3-5 business days. For additional artifacts like HSM diagrams or private deployment runbooks it might be a week. We'll prioritize SOC 2 and the SSO/KMS diagrams.
[05:42] Ethan: For the KMS integration deep-dive we need to know whether keys ever leave our control in hosted mode.
[05:47] Priya: In hosted mode using Redwood-managed keys, the key material is managed by Redwood/KMS vendor. For BYOK the key material remains under your control and we call the KMS for encryption/decryption operations without persisting key material. We'll provide a flow diagram.
[05:59] Sarah: Any known gaps that Aperture should be worried about?
[06:02] Jared: Nothing critical. A couple of items to watch: log retention beyond default needs an add-on, and if you require HSM for all environments we might need a private deployment. We'll flag these in the SIG.
[06:14] Priya: One more note - in the SIG there's a mis-labeled control referencing "KV cache encryption" - we'll fix the mismatch and attach a clarifying note.
[06:23] Maya: Perfect. Let's confirm next steps.
[06:26] Jared: Action items: Jared to upload completed SIG spreadsheet and evidence bundle to the Box folder by 2026-07-14. Priya to send KMS architecture and RBAC matrix by 2026-07-16. Ethan to send any Clarifying SOC 2 questions by 2026-07-17. We'll reconvene for a KMS/keys deep-dive week of 2026-07-20.
[06:47] Sarah: Works for me. Thanks all.
[06:50] Jared: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and calendar invite for the deep-dive.
[06:55] Priya: Thanks.
[06:57] End of recording.
